Thermoplastics, like polythene and PVC, soften when heated and can be moulded again and again, so they can be recycled. Plastics that cannot be remoulded or melted, like bakelite, are thermosetting plastics. So options (1), (3) and (4) describe thermosetting plastics, and option (2) is true only if 'destroyed' means 'deformed' (softened) by heating.
